headline: Paramount+ growth accelerates as deal costs squeeze earnings
summary_short: Paramount Skydance's Q2 FY2026 revenue was roughly flat y/y at $6.91B (+0.9%) as 16% Paramount+ growth offset a continued TV Media decline, while net income fell 28% y/y to $41M on $153M of WBD-deal transaction costs and higher interest expense; the company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $3.8-3.9B.
summary_long: Revenue of $6.91B was roughly flat y/y (+0.9%) and down 5.9% q/q, as 9% DTC growth (Paramount+ +16% on subscriber and ARPU gains) and 16% Studios growth were largely offset by a 9% TV Media decline. Operating income fell to $475M, including $153M of WBD-transaction costs; net income fell 28% y/y to $41M as higher interest expense ($255M) and a doubled tax provision ($120M) outweighed the operating gains. Adjusted EBITDA rose 27% y/y to $1.10B (15.9% margin), and free cash flow rose to $258M. Cash fell to $1.63B q/q after a $2.8B advance payment tied to the pending Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition. Management raised FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $3.8-3.9B and guided Q3 revenue to $6.95-7.15B.

drivers.explanation: Total revenue +1% y/y and -6% q/q; DTC (+9%) and Studios (+16%) growth were largely offset by a continued decline in TV Media revenue.

DTC revenue +9% y/y, led by Paramount+ +16% on ~6% subscriber growth and ~12% ARPU growth, driven by the FIFA World Cup, UFC and Originals programming that delivered the platform's lowest-churn quarter.

Studios revenue +16% y/y on a strong quarter of third-party TV Studios deliveries and consolidated Skydance licensing revenue, partly offset by lower theatrical revenue lapping Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning.
TV Media revenue -9% y/y: advertising -14% on NCAA lapping and the Telefe/Chilevision sale, partly offset by political advertising; affiliate revenue -6% on continued pay-TV subscriber erosion.
Operating income of $475M (6.9% margin) includes $153M of transaction-related costs tied to the pending Warner Bros. Discovery combination.

Net earnings fell y/y and q/q despite higher operating income, as interest expense rose to $255M and the tax provision more than doubled to $120M; the release does not attribute this to a specific cause.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 27% y/y to $1.1B, with profitability improving across all three segments (DTC, Studios, TV Media).
